title: Vehicle Service Contracts Claim Adjudication Standard
content:
A repair claim under a Vehicle Service Contract is either authorized or denied by the administrator, DriveSure Administrative Services, LLC, against the standard below. The service contract's status, enrollment date, odometer at sale, expiration date and expiration odometer are read from the service contract record.

## 1. Status

A repair claim is adjudicated only on a service contract whose status is active. A cancelled or expired service contract carries no adjudication.

## 2. Waiting period

A breakdown is covered only when the repair date is later than the enrollment date plus the plan's waiting period in days. The waiting period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the enrollment date, and the odometer on the repair order must also exceed the odometer at sale plus the plan's waiting period in miles.

Both parts are strict: a repair dated on the last day of the waiting period is not later than it, and an odometer equal to the odometer at sale plus the waiting-period miles does not exceed it.

| Hypothetical service contract: enrolled 1 June, odometer at sale 40000 miles, waiting period 30 calendar days and 1000 miles | Date part | Mileage part |
|---|---|---|
| Repair dated 1 July (day 30, counting 2 June as day 1), odometer 41000 | not later than 1 July: not met | 41000 does not exceed 41000: not met |
| Repair dated 2 July, odometer 41001 | later than 1 July: met | 41001 exceeds 41000: met |

## 3. One decision per repair order

A repair order is adjudicated once: on one service contract, a repair order number that already carries an authorization or a denial is not adjudicated again.

## 4. Authorization or denial

The claim is authorized when all of the following hold:

1. the failed part belongs to the plan's covered component groups and not to the listed exclusions;
2. the failure did not begin before enrollment or during the waiting period;
3. the repair is done at a facility meeting the plan's repair facility rule that obtained authorization first;
4. where a lubricated part failed, the maintenance records meet the plan's oil-change interval;
5. the repair order odometer is below the expiration odometer and the repair date is on or before the expiration date.

Otherwise it is denied with the first failing reason in this order: not covered component, waiting period, expired coverage, no preauthorization, missing maintenance records, lifetime limit reached.

*Hypothetical denials.* A claim for a part outside the covered component groups, repaired without prior authorization, is denied for not covered component, the first failing reason in the order. A claim whose only failing point is that the claims paid have reached the lifetime claim limit is denied for lifetime limit reached.

*Expiry boundary (hypothetical expiration odometer 77000 miles).* A repair order at 76999 miles is below the expiration odometer; one at 77000 miles is not. A repair dated on the expiration date itself is on or before it.

## 5. Decision time

A complete claim is decided within the plan's number of business days for authorizing or denying a complete claim.

## 6. What the decision records

An authorization is recorded per repair order with the authorization date, the repair order number, the repair facility, the odometer on the repair order, the covered component group repaired, the amount authorized (covered parts, labor and diagnosis, before the deductible) and the deductible charged to the borrower. A denial is recorded per repair order with the denial date, the repair order number, the repair facility, the odometer on the repair order, the component group claimed and the reason for the denial.
